project.name: unihack8
project.description: Mobile app for Timisoara (Connected Communities hackathon): filterable map, live STPT transit, events with QR check-in and reliability points, and an AI guide, built with Expo React Native and a Spring Boot + Supabase backend.

tour.title: What the project is for
tour.description: Start with AGENTS.md: it states the Connected Communities problem, the feature list (filterable map, live STPT transit, directions, an AI guide, user-created events with QR check-in and reliability points) and the working rules every change must follow. DOCS.md then shows how the Expo app, the Spring Boot API, Supabase and the external data sources fit together and what is actually built today.

tour.title: The roadmap and the API contract
tour.description: PLAN.md splits the work into 17 tasks over three tracks (A backend and events, B city data and AI, C mobile). Most of it is still unticked, so it shows what remains to be built. docs/API.md is the contract the mobile track should mock against, and it covers only the users endpoints so far.

tour.title: Backend entry point and build
tour.description: BackendApplication starts the Spring Boot API. The Gradle build pins Spring Boot 4.1.2 on Java 21 with the JPA, Security, OAuth2 resource-server and validation starters, and application.properties pulls secrets from an optional, git-ignored application-local.properties whose keys are listed in the committed .example file.
tour.languageLesson: Spring Boot's @SpringBootApplication combines auto-configuration, component scanning and configuration in one annotation; the properties file is where datasource and JWT settings are wired in.

tour.title: Security: validating Supabase tokens
tour.description: SecurityConfig makes the API stateless, disables CSRF, enables CORS and leaves only GET requests for events, places and transit public; everything else needs a valid Supabase JWT checked against the project's JWKS URL. CurrentUser turns the token's subject claim into the profile UUID that controllers use.
tour.languageLesson: In a Spring Security resource server the SecurityFilterChain bean defines which routes are open; the verified JWT is then injected into controller methods as a Jwt object.

tour.title: The users HTTP endpoints
tour.description: UserController exposes GET /users/me, PATCH /users/me, GET /users/search and GET /users/{id}, delegating to UserService. The request and response records (UpdateUsernameRequest, ProfileResponse) are the payload shapes described in docs/API.md.

tour.title: Turning failures into JSON errors
tour.description: The service throws small exceptions (user not found, username taken, invalid search) and UserExceptionHandler converts each into an ApiError with a stable code and the matching HTTP status, such as 404 USER_NOT_FOUND or 409 USERNAME_TAKEN, so the mobile app can show precise messages.

tour.title: Profile business logic
tour.description: UserService defines the operations and UserServiceImpl implements them: loading own and public profiles with attended events, changing a username after a case-insensitive uniqueness check, and a username-prefix search capped at 20 results. ProfileMapper turns entities and event summaries into the response records.
tour.languageLesson: The project's package convention puts an interface next to an impl/ folder holding the implementation, for service, mapper and repository alike.

tour.title: Persistence against Supabase
tour.description: Profile is the JPA entity for the profiles table and ProfileRepository adds case-insensitive username lookups. AttendedEventRepository and its JDBC implementation read events a user actually attended from the event tables that are being created separately in Supabase, so live integration is still pending.

tour.title: How the backend is tested
tour.description: Tests never touch Supabase: UserControllerTest uses MockMvc with a fake JWT, UserServiceImplTest mocks the repositories with Mockito, ProfileRepositoryTest runs queries on in-memory H2, and BackendApplicationTests checks that the whole context starts.

tour.title: The mobile app shell and map screen
tour.description: The Expo app uses file-based routing: _layout.jsx sets up the navigation stack and index.jsx is the map screen centred on Timisoara with a Locate me button that asks for location permission only when tapped. app.json and package.json set the Expo SDK 54 configuration and dependencies.
tour.languageLesson: With Expo Router every file under src/app is a route, and _layout.jsx wraps the screens in a navigator.

tour.title: Mobile helpers and their tests
tour.description: map.js holds Timisoara's coordinates and a validated region builder used by the map screen, while api.js is a small GET client driven by EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL that no screen uses yet. setup.test.mjs covers both helpers with Node's built-in test runner.
